name: Electro House
about: Electro house is the loud, distorted, mid-2000s strain of house: saw-wave basslines, compressed kicks, big-room drops and a sense of humour about all of it. Benny Benassi's Satisfaction in 2002 set the sound, and Paris's Ed Banger label, Berlin's Boys Noize, Melbourne's Bang Gang and Toronto's MSTRKRFT made it the club music of the indie-dance years, with Justice, Digitalism and Simian Mobile Disco turning it into albums. Deadmau5, Wolfgang Gartner and the Dutch producers around Afrojack and Chuckie then carried it into the EDM festival boom, where it became big-room house and lost most of its grit. Its peak is 2006 to 2009, and the best records from those years still sound like a party.

artists.name: Simian Mobile Disco
artists.why: analogue electro house with pop hooks

albums.title: Kittenz and Thee Glitz
albums.why: Silver Screen Shower Scene and Miss Kittin's deadpan vocals made the electroclash record that electro house grew out of; still sharp.

albums.title: Hypnotica
albums.why: Satisfaction's distorted saw bass invented the genre's sound, and the album around it is the same trick done a dozen enjoyable ways.

albums.title: Destroy Rock & Roll
albums.why: A bedroom-made Scottish record of filtered pop samples and chunky electro grooves; Drop the Pressure and the title track defined a British summer.

albums.title: Devin Dazzle & the Neon Fever
albums.why: The follow-up swaps electroclash for glam-synth electro house, with Rocket Ride and Ready 2 Wear; slighter, but it rolls.

albums.title: Nite Versions
albums.why: The Dewaele brothers remade their own rock album as a continuous electro house set, and E Talking and NY Excuse became the scene's anthems.

albums.title: Sexor
albums.why: The Turbo Recordings boss's debut is sleazy, hook-heavy electro house with a Montreal sense of humour; You Gonna Want Me is the one.

albums.title: The Looks
albums.why: Jesse Keeler and Al-P's debut turned Death from Above's bass distortion into electro house, with Easy Love and Work on You.
Compressed, distorted and sampled from chopped disco and prog, the Ed Banger duo's debut is electro house's masterpiece, with D.A.N.C.E. and Phantom.

albums.title: Idealism
albums.why: Pogo and Zdarlight married electro house to indie-rock hooks, and the Hamburg duo's debut was the crossover record of its year.

albums.title: Attack Decay Sustain Release
albums.why: Analogue synths, chanted vocals and real songs; Hustler and It's the Beat made SMD the British face of the sound.

albums.title: Oi Oi Oi
albums.why: Alex Ridha's debut is the Berlin electro house record, hard, distorted and funky, with &Down and Lava Lava as club staples.

albums.title: Random Album Title
albums.why: Ghosts 'n' Stuff and I Remember sit between electro house and the progressive revival, and the album made Joel Zimmerman the scene's biggest name.

albums.title: Lambs Anger
albums.why: Quentin Dupieux's Ed Banger album is electro house at its most warped and funny, with Positif and Pourriture as the keepers.

albums.title: Power
albums.why: Louder and more techno-leaning than the debut, Power carries Jeffer and Kontakt Me; a strong second record from the scene's hardest producer.

albums.title: Romborama
albums.why: Sir Bob Cornelius Rifo's masked punk-electro album is relentless and crude, with Warp 1.9 as the hit; important to the EDM crossover, exhausting in full.

albums.title: Fist of God
albums.why: Heavier and rap-heavy, with Heartbreaker and John Legend; the second MSTRKRFT album chases the charts and loses some of the fun.

albums.title: Tons of Friends
albums.why: The Italian duo's guest-stuffed debut brought fidget house's wobble to a wider audience; patchy, but the energy is real.

albums.title: 4x4=12
albums.why: Some Chords and Raise Your Weapon are the bridge between electro house and the EDM festival sound, and the album is Deadmau5's most complete.

albums.title: Total
albums.why: The Ed Banger producer's debut is a dense, distorted electro house record with Embody and Tetra; late to the party, but the best-produced of the lot.

albums.title: Weekend in America
albums.why: Gartner's maximal, intricately programmed electro house got a full album with will.i.am and Eve guest spots; the instrumentals are the reason to listen.

albums.title: Audio, Video, Disco
albums.why: Justice swapped distortion for prog-rock pastiche, and the result is a divisive but well-made record with Civilization as its hit.

albums.title: Clarity
albums.why: The title track took electro house to pop radio, and Anton Zaslavski's debut is the most song-driven record of the EDM wave.

albums.title: The Rules of Dada
albums.why: The Swedish duo's festival-sized electro house is big, dumb and self-aware, with Kick Out the Epic Motherf**ker as the mission statement.

albums.title: Adventure
albums.why: Hugo Leclercq's debut is electro house as bright French pop, with Pay No Mind and You're On; a late, melodic coda to the genre.
